population.rule: items that carry the manifest's settlement_item_field

declaration.author: Reticuli
declaration.timing_basis: Written on 2026-11-12, after the bank's result was filed. The generator and its seeds were committed before the mint; this record was not.

construction.description: 144 world skeletons (6 domains x 24, sizes 2 to 8, 12 frames, 6 tasks per domain) are fixed by the code. One seed draws the names, scores and orders inside each world; a second seed deals the worlds to the two forms by rejection sampling under balance rules.
construction.seed_basis: World seed and assignment seed are constants of the generator at the pinned commit. The manifest's own seed is the run seed and is neither of them.

seeds.name: world
seeds.decides: names, scores, weighted member and option orders inside each world; the text of every calibration item
seeds.stream: one per world, keyed by seed and world id

seeds.name: assignment
seeds.decides: which form each world is rendered in
seeds.stream: one for the whole bank, with rejection

seeds.name: run
seeds.decides: the deal of arms to readers and the resampling; nothing in the bank

dimensions.definition: Literal committed settlement stratum. Its membership is the outcome of the seeded assignment.
Literal committed frame family: which of twelve opening sentences the item carries.
Literal committed size of the item's set.
Exact complete English and marked string templates; one per form and frame.

key.english:
A change request has arrived for {task}; the on-call engineer is checking what it permits.
The frozen roster lists these eligible {member_type} identities, in recorded order: {members}. Recorded {criterion} scores, in the same order: {scores}. The reference {set_ref} resolves uniquely to this finite, nonempty snapshot of distinct identities. The snapshot was fixed before any selection, and {outsider} is not in it. Nothing else has been required of the selection, and no outcome has been observed yet. Each distinct identity is one member; repeated appearances do not create another member.
Request: choose-any({set_ref}) requires {set_ref} to resolve uniquely to a finite, nonempty set of distinct eligible member identities. It denotes choosing exactly one member of {set_ref} and explicitly makes every member acceptable; the selection policy is otherwise unconstrained. A deterministic first-member rule, a cost- or latency-based rule, a weighted rule, or a uniform draw can all satisfy choose-any. The form therefore makes no claim of randomness, equal probability, unpredictability, independence, rotation, or fairness.
